steps.body: Numbers **break apart**! 5 can split into 2 and 3 — or 1 and 4. Both pairs make 5.

widget.prompt: 5 splits into 1 and MORE. 1 dot is here. Tap the rest of the 5.

commonCounts.feedback: One dot short — 1 and 4 make 5, so fill to 5.
One too many — stop at 5 in all.

widget.missFeedback: 1 is placed. 5 needs 4 more: 1 and 4 make 5.

steps.body: One number, many splits. 6 breaks into 5 and 1, or 4 and 2, or 3 and 3.

widget.prompt: 6 crayons split between two boxes. One box has 4 — they are already in the frame. Add dots until the frame shows all 6.

commonCounts.feedback: 4 and 4 make 8 — too many. The other box holds 2.
6 is the whole — the other PART is 2.
4 and 3 make 7 — one too many. It is 2.

widget.missFeedback: The locked dots are the box of 4 — add just enough to show the whole 6.

explanationVariants: 3 and 3 make 6 — a double split, both parts equal.

widget.prompt: 6 cherries shared EQUALLY between two bowls. How many in each bowl?

options.feedback: Yes — 3 and 3 make 6, a perfectly even split.
6 in each would be 12 — equal shares of 6 are 3 and 3.
2 and 2 make only 4 — six splits into 3 and 3.
4 and 4 make 8 — too many. Equal parts of 6 are 3 each.

explanationVariants: 8 breaks into 6 and 2 — count on from 6: 7, 8.

commonCounts.feedback: 6 and 3 make 9 — one too many. It is 2.

widget.missFeedback: The locked dots are the tower of 6 — add just enough to show the whole 8.

explanationVariants: 1 and 3 make only 4 — every true split of 5 adds to 5.
Check each pair: only 1 and 3 fails to make 5.

widget.prompt: Which pair is NOT a split of 5?

options.label: 2 and 3
options.feedback: 2 and 3 DO make 5 — that split works.

options.label: 1 and 4
options.feedback: 1 and 4 DO make 5 — that split works.

options.label: 0 and 5
options.feedback: 0 and 5 make 5 — even zero can be a part!

hints: Check each pair: do the parts make 5?
2 and 3? Yes. 1 and 4? Yes. 0 and 5? Yes.
1 and 3 make only 4 — that pair fails.

steps.body: Numbers break into parts many ways. Parts joined make the whole again.
takeaways: A number splits into pairs of parts: 5 is 2 and 3, or 1 and 4.
Equal splits share evenly: 6 is 3 and 3.
Adding, taking away, splitting — you can do it all to 10!
steps.teaser: One big idea is left — how to MAKE TEN!

concept.body: A number breaks into two parts. 5 splits into 2 and 3 — the parts make the whole again.

widget.prompt: 5 candies split between two hands. One hand has 2. How many in the other?

options.feedback: 5 is the whole — the other hand holds 3.
2 and 2 make only 4 — the other hand holds 3.
2 and 4 make 6 — one too many. It is 3.
